payload_sans_images.prompt: Viewed from directly overhead, straight down: the stone floor of an ancient jungle temple. Large weathered cobblestones and flagstones, uneven and cracked, each stone big and clearly readable, moss darkening the seams between stones, exactly as in the reference frame. Off-center, toward the lower right, a burning wooden torch lies dropped on the stones: its flame burns hard and restlessly, whipping sideways, flaring up bright and shrinking back with the wind, and the wide pool of warm torchlight PULSES with every flare - long soft shadows off the stones' edges visibly swing and breathe across the floor as the flame moves. Embers spray from the flame every second or two and skitter fast and glowing across the stone before winking out; a thick curl of smoke rolls quickly low across the flagstones, coiling and tearing in the wind. Gusts keep dry fallen leaves skittering and tumbling across the stones throughout. The rest of the floor sits in dim, even ambient light that the moving torchlight visibly plays into. The stone floor fills the entire frame and continues beyond every edge - no border, no curb, no wall, no edging: nothing but floor. Absolutely locked static camera, perfectly perpendicular top-down view: no zoom, no pan, no rotation, no tilt, no parallax, no depth of field. Flame, shadow, embers, smoke or leaves are visibly moving at every moment; continuous motion from the first frame to the last. No people, no animals, no text, no watermark.
